fit.note: Moments of a 10-day realized-variance proxy, so kappa and xi come out biased: the bootstrap (200 simulated histories from this fit) measures how much. Daily closes barely identify rho; equity option markets typically imply about -0.7. v0 is the trailing 21-day realized variance.

Jumps carry 74% of the return variance, the share the data identify best. 182 jumps a year of about 1.7% each: the likelihood is describing fat daily tails with frequent small jumps, not rare crashes.

Regimes 0 = Bear (39 days), 1 = Sideways (975 days), 2 = Bull (239 days). Days are labelled bear after a 20% drawdown from the 60-day high and bull after a 20% rally off the 60-day low; regimes that never occur are omitted. A regime's drift over a few weeks is mostly noise: read it with its error.
Parameters are per day. Long-run volatility 26.0% a year; a variance shock halves in 14 trading days (persistence 0.950).

H and eta come from how fast log|returns| decorrelate across lags, above a noise floor (pi^2/4 for Gaussian shocks; fitted here). Daily closes barely identify roughness: the bootstrap spread of H says how little. The rho proxy is strongly attenuated toward 0 (in simulations a true -0.7 reads as about -0.1). xi0 is the trailing 21-day realized variance.
